aria: Animated recap of the Pistons' 113 to 98 home win over the Bucks: Daniss Jenkins' 39-foot 3-pointer at the third-quarter buzzer that made it 90 to 76, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Isaiah Joe's 22 points off the bench, the top scorers, how the Pistons won, and the next game.

notes: Box score from StatMuse's game page for the Pistons' 113–98 home win over Milwaukee on Nov 27, 2026, an NBA Cup group game: all 113 Detroit points and all 98 Milwaukee points add up from the player lines, as do the shooting totals (40 of 93, 16 of 47 from three, 17 of 25 FT for Detroit; 38 of 87, 12 of 40, 10 of 13 for Milwaukee) and steals (12–8). Hoops Nightly matches every player's points and shooting, and the quarter scores (24–24–42–23 to 29–21–26–22) are on StatMuse, Hoops Nightly and Digest Sports. Milwaukee led 50–48 at the half; Detroit led 90–76 after three (StatMuse play-by-play, SB Nation's Rapid Recap; one AP version says 90–78, which doesn't match the line score). Bench points (60–32) add up from the box and are on Hoops Nightly; fast-break points (24–11), points in the paint (38–50) and the biggest leads (Detroit 20, Milwaukee 16, at 19–3) are from Hoops Nightly, and Field Level Media also has Detroit's 20. Rebound totals differ between sources, so they aren't used, nor are Harkless' assists (7 or 8). Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Friday's games.

Detroit played without Cade Cunningham (right knee, second straight game; Field Level Media). Its bench outscored its starters 60–53 (AP; The Detroit News). Isaiah Joe scored 22 with five 3-pointers, his second straight 20-point game and second straight with five threes, and Elijah Harkless' 14 points were a career high (Detroit Free Press). Detroit finished 3–1 and won East Group A on point differential over Toronto and Orlando, reaching the NBA Cup knockout round for the first time; it hosts Boston in the quarterfinals on Dec 5 (Yahoo Sports). Milwaukee finished 0–4. Rookie Brayden Burries scored 23 off the bench for Milwaukee (StatMuse). Next: Detroit hosts Orlando on Sunday (Hoops Nightly; Free Press); Milwaukee hosts Oklahoma City on Saturday (AP; Hoops Nightly).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Daniss Jenkins' 3-pointer from Elijah Harkless at the third-quarter buzzer that made it 90–76: StatMuse's play-by-play has a "39' pullup three" with the assist from Harkless and Digest Sports a 39-foot three, right after Myles Turner's three with a second left made it 87–76. The Detroit News calls it "a long three from near half-court" and the AP "a buzzer-beating three." So the board's Pistons +11 to +14 is 87–76 to 90–76. The defender isn't described, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from deep. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Detroit Pistons or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Jenkins' listed 6-foot-4 and 165 pounds (Basketball-Reference; Wikipedia), in the Pistons' home white with No. 24 (Wikipedia). No wingspan is reported, so his arms are at the default length. He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn in the kit with the default skin tone. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
